sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — Gemini API
sources.evidence: Identifies stable gemini-3.1-flash-lite. Lists 1,048,576 input tokens, 65,536 output tokens, text/image/video/audio/PDF input, text output, thinking and function calling. Describes low latency and high-volume workflows. Reopened October 27, 2026; the stable-model specification table gives no numerical total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — May 7 and March 3, 2026
sources.evidence: May 7 explicitly releases gemini-3.1-flash-lite as GA. March 3 launches Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Preview; May 25 shuts down gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview in favor of the stable model.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — Google Cloud model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model ID is gemini-3.1-flash-lite, with GA release May 7, 2026. Independently lists 1,048,576 context, 65,536 maximum output, thinking, function calling and multimodal input.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Model Card — updated May 2026
sources.evidence: Reopened the complete May 2026 PDF on October 27, 2026. Its dependency and architecture sections explicitly identify Gemini 3 Pro as the base; it gives no numerical total or active count. The evaluation tables contain capability and safety measures, not parameter sizes.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro Model Card — updated May 2026
sources.evidence: Reopened the complete May 2026 Pro card on October 27, 2026. It names Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite among its dependent models and describes sparse MoE routing qualitatively. Neither a nominal total, activated count, expert count nor routing width is disclosed for the base or Flash-Lite. The named lineage is explicit, but no supported base size is available to inherit.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite Model Card — July 21, 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 review of the complete July card, architecture and exact-name comparison table. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite explicitly names 3.1 Flash-Lite as its base; the comparison provides prices and benchmark scores, and safety comparisons provide percentage changes. No total or activated-parameter column or count is supplied.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Service use requires Google API and Gemini terms; terms prohibit extraction or replication of underlying model weights. Supports the proprietary API-access classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite evaluation methodology — March 2026
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview as the Gemini API ID used for March evaluations. Does not establish that the later GA checkpoint is unchanged.

sources.title: Vertex AI release notes — March 3, 2026
sources.evidence: Historical March 3 entry calls the model public preview while writing the unsuffixed gemini-3.1-flash-lite ID. This conflicts with preview-versus-stable API naming, and does not explicitly bridge unchanged checkpoint identity to GA.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash Model Card — September 2, 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 later-disclosure check of the complete current card. Its dependency is 3.7 Flash and its comparisons give no retrospective numerical total or active count for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Card — October 13, 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 later-disclosure check of the complete decoded card. Argon is a new model, not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model; no total or active parameter count for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite appears.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — HTML model card
sources.evidence: Linked by the stable API documentation. HTML remains dated March 3, while its downloadable PDF is updated May 2026; both refer architecture to Gemini 3 Pro. Reopened October 27: the explicit dependency statement names Gemini 3 Pro, but neither the HTML nor PDF provides a count.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 review of the complete report text for parameter disclosures and Flash-Lite references. Monitoring experiments use 3.5 Flash-Lite, and parameter occurrences concern evaluation difficulty, model security or encoded knowledge. No retrospective total or active count for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is supplied.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite: Built for intelligence at scale
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the March 3, 2026 original preview launch during the October 27 parameter re-audit. It describes relative model tiers, price, speed and capability comparisons without a numerical total or active count. Faster output and lower price are not parameter-count evidence, and this preview post does not establish unchanged checkpoint identity with the May stable release.

name.note: Use the official hyphenated display name.

developer.note: Google product, with model documentation published by Google DeepMind.

family.note: Catalog-normalized Flash-Lite subfamily within Gemini 3; the official later Flash-Lite card identifies this model as its base.

release_date.note: Exact stable release. March 3 was public preview; older Vertex notes use the unsuffixed ID for that preview. No inspected source explicitly states the preview and GA checkpoints are unchanged, so March is not transferred to this stable record.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted API/product access under Google terms; no downloadable-weight distribution is provided.

license.note: Descriptive classification for hosted access under Google service terms; not an SPDX open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model and exact-ID count/lineage searches, original model cards and API page, and later Google comparisons found no supported nominal total. The named Gemini 3 Pro base is explicit, but no published count for that base was found. Neither price/speed comparisons nor generic model-tier language supplies a number. Null reflects absent numerical evidence, not a requirement for an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-parameter searches and later comparison-table checks found no numerical active count for this model or its named Pro base. Sparse expert routing is documented without expert dimensions or routing width. The later exact-name tables give performance, price and safety, not activated parameters; no active count is inferred from total size or efficiency claims.

architecture.note: The stable documentation links this exact card; its architecture section explicitly delegates to Gemini 3 Pro, which specifies a sparse MoE Transformer. This is an explicit documentation chain, not a family-name inference. Expert counts and routing details remain unspecified.

context_window.note: Documented Gemini API input-token limit; Google Cloud also labels this the context window. The separate maximum output is 65,536 tokens. This is an endpoint specification, not a claim about training context or current callability.

modalities.note: Exact stable API page lists these supported data types. PDF is retained as the documented document input type; image/audio/video generation is not asserted.

reasoning.note: Thinking is explicitly supported; Cloud lists minimal, low, medium and high levels.

tool_call.note: Function calling is explicitly supported for the stable model.

description.value: Low-latency Gemini model for high-volume multimodal and agent workloads
description.note: The description is supported by the exact-model developer guide and needs no correction.

patch.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
patch.notes: Stable release: May 7, 2026. March 3 was a preview; historical Vertex notes used the unsuffixed name, but unchanged preview-to-stable checkpoint identity is not established. Sparse MoE Transformer based on Gemini 3 Pro; total and active parameter counts are undisclosed for both this model and its named base.
